accepted_edits.reason: the edits are the answers recorded against the content and design findings of 22 November

findings.reason: the node's gate can never pass as written, and because the plan names no owner and declares no wait for the two excluded failures, a dispatched worker will either report blocked on work it was told not to do or edit a file outside its write paths.
findings.text: s38's head arm is "the population `grep -l pending_landing tests/*.py` runs on all_debug at the node's head with no failure", but the section's own Why puts that population at "252 passed and 8 failed" and sets two of the eight aside as "a regression from that day's measurement-release landing and are repaired separately"; the set I measured is exactly the base log's 34 files, and `test_an_existing_landing_owner_is_not_bypassed` still fails both its parameters at HEAD `ee81ed54` (`2 failed, 10 deselected in 2.26s`), so no node restricted to s38's declared write paths and its six named ids can reach a green population

findings.reason: the followup is the chain's next-work statement, so a coordinator reading it re-queues six completed sections and never learns that five new sections are awaiting dispatch.
findings.text: the driving followup's body now reads "§34 is delivered and the rest are queued.a-claim-nobody-is-working-is-released.", which (a) contradicts `plan-section-declarations` at plan.html:23, where s31, s32, s33, s35, s36 and s37 are `done`, (b) omits §38 to §42, which the same snapshot declares `implementable`, and (c) leaves a bare plan slug after a full stop where the previous sentence that introduced it was dropped

findings.reason: a worker held to the declared write paths cannot tell a gate that never started from one the merge broke, so the node's second deliverable — the one that makes `.venv/bin/python` run at the merged head — returns to the coordinator as a scope blocker, or is implemented out of scope.
findings.text: s41's write paths are `reckon/crew/landing_measure.py` and `reckon/crew/promotion.py`, but both behaviours it asks for are decided in `reckon/crew/promotion_gate.py`: the merged-head replay executes the command through `sh -c` at `promotion_gate.py:1019` (so exit 127 is observed there) and `_merged_gate_finding` at `promotion_gate.py:552-608` composes the very sentence the section quotes, "the merge changes what this node's gate proves"

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/{pending_landing,promotion_requests,promotion,promotion_scope,landing_measure,queue_landing}.py`, `reckon/crew_run_commands.py`, the three cited test files, all five cited plan slugs, commits `abb8ea8fd8` and `204509cf6f` and error strings quoted from `promotion.py:1999`, `promotion.py:2400`, `ledger.py:4032` and `promotion_gate.py:595` all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — s38's head arm requires the whole `pending_landing` population green at the node's head, while the section itself excludes two of that population's eight failures as "repaired separately" — 2 failed, 10 deselected at HEAD `ee81ed54` on `tests/test_a_merged_promoted_run_is_released.py` — and no section in this plan owns that repair.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every arm's log is declared under the run directory, and s38's cited base log exists at `~/.cache/reckon-portfolio/owner-check/base.log` (31,621 bytes, header names `abb8ea8fd8` and a literal command, closing line `8 failed, 252 passed`).
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new sections name no symbol, stage label or ticket number, and their write paths use the file names the repository already carries.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the driving followup's body states that §34 is delivered and "the rest are queued", while the plan's own declarations mark §31, §32, §33, §35, §36 and §37 `done`, and it names no section after §37.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of s38 to s42 states one deliverable, and s41's two clauses (report a gate that cannot start; resolve a relative interpreter) are both measured by its first done-when arm, so one gate closes the node.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s39's and s40's upstreams (§15 restore, the promotion service's tick) are landed, and s39–s42 declare no relationship that points at a wrong node; the gap that s38 cannot be dispatched to a passable gate is reported under done_when, because no existing node can be depended on.
